{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from PBS

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# PBS resources:
#   -P CBBI1106
#   -N array_job
#   -l select=1:ncpus=24
#   -l walltime=1:00:00
#   -o /mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/oe_files/array_job_m1.out
#   -e /mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/oe_files/array_job_m1.err
#   -J 1-21:21
#   -q smp
#   -M belindalombard@sun.ac.za
#   -m be

#flux: --job-name=array_job
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 24
#flux: --time-limit=1h
#flux: --output=/mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/oe_files/array_job_m1.out
#flux: --error=/mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/oe_files/array_job_m1.err

# Omitted PBS option: -J 1-21:21 (job array)
# Flux job arrays are not available as a universally portable batch-script directive.
# Performance implication: you must submit separate jobs manually (or wrap a loop), increasing scheduler overhead and potentially reducing throughput.

# Omitted PBS option: -P CBBI1106 (project/account)
# Flux accounting/project selection is site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may be charged to a default account or be rejected by policy.

# Omitted PBS option: -q smp (queue)
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run with different priority/limits or be rejected by policy.

# Omitted PBS options: -M / -m (email notifications)
# Flux does not provide a universal, built-in email notification directive in batch scripts.
# Performance implication: none on runtime performance, but you will not receive automatic job emails.

sleep 4

module add chpc/R/3.5.1-gcc7.2.0

cd /mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/

make sbv

# PBS_ARRAY_INDEX is not set under Flux. Default to 1 if not provided.
# You may pass a start index as the first argument when launching the script.
PBS_ARRAY_INDEX=${1:-1}

STEP=21
START=$PBS_ARRAY_INDEX
END=$(( START + STEP - 1 ))

for i in $(eval echo "{$START..$END}")
do
  (echo "process $i started" && Rscript sbv/method_1_analysis/method_1_arrayjob.R $i && echo "process $i finished") &
done

sleep 0.1
echo "Waiting for processes to finish"
wait $(jobs -p)
echo "All processes finished"
"
}
